#2016. Elche vs Real Betis - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 06 Nov 2026 14:48, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 14:51

Real Betis will aim to make it successive wins in Spain's top flight when they continue their campaign against Elche at Estadio Martinez Valero on Sunday afternoon.

The visitors posted a 2-1 victory over Malaga in their last league match, while Elche will enter the contest off the back of a 1-0 home defeat to Valencia.

Elche boast a record of two wins, four draws and five defeats from their 11 league matches this season, with 10 points leaving them in 17th spot in the La Liga table.

The Green-Striped Ones were beaten 1-0 by Valencia in their last match, but that proved to be their first loss in five games in all competitions.

Martin Anselmi's side have actually won two of their last three matches, including a 3-1 victory over Pinatar in the Copa del Rey at the end of October.

Elche have struggled in their recent meetings with Real Betis, losing four of the last five fixtures between the two sides, but the corresponding game last season finished 1-1.

The Green-Striped Ones have not managed to overcome Real Betis since April 2022, while their last home success over the Seville outfit came back in November 2009.

Real Betis lead the overall head-to-head record between the two sides, having posted 24 wins to Elche's 16, while 17 of their 57 games have finished all square.

Manuel Pellegrini's side were in Champions League action during the week, suffering a 2-1 defeat to Borussia Dortmund in the league stage of the competition.

The Seville outfit were 2-1 winners over Malaga last time out, with that success making their record seven wins, two draws and two defeats from their 11 league matches this season, which has left them fourth in the table on 23 points.

Real Betis are only four points off third-placed Real Madrid and are, as expected, firmly in the Champions League picture at this stage of the La Liga campaign.

El Glorioso have a record of two wins, two draws and one defeat from their five away league matches this season, scoring six times and conceding seven.

Elche will be without the services of Marc Aguado and Thomas Lemar for this weekend's match through injury, but the home side are otherwise in strong form.

Yago Santiago and Gonzalo Villar had both been doubts for this contest, but the pair are available for selection, while Pedro Bigas should also again be in the squad.

Lemar's position in the starting side is likely to be taken by Facundo Buonanotte, while there will be a spot through the middle for Fer Nino, who has netted six times in La Liga this season.

As for Real Betis, Cucho Hernandez remains on the sidelines and is unlikely to be back in the fold for the Seville outfit until the end of November.

Facundo Bernal is still suspended, but Junior Firpo and Alvaro Fidalgo are both expected to be back in the squad after recent absences.

Troy Parrott has not scored for Real Betis since the start of September, but the 24-year-old is expected to continue through the middle for Pellegrini's team.

Dituro; Sangare, Chust, Redondo, Revivo; Villar, Morcillo; Cepeda, Buonanotte, Valera; Nino

Valles; Bellerin, Bartra, Natan, Garcia; Roca, Fornals; Antony, Isco, Ezzalzouli; Parrott

Elche have been in solid form of late, and this is not a straightforward match for Real Betis, but we are backing the Seville outfit to secure a valuable three points on Sunday.

#2014. Chelsea predicted lineup vs. Sunderland: Emi Martinez, Moises Caicedo decisions made

By Ben Knapton | 06 Nov 2026 14:58

Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez is in contention to make his return from injury in Sunday's Premier League clash with Sunderland at the Stadium of Light.

The Argentina international has made an excellent recovery from his sickening head collision with Everton's Jarrad Branthwaite, which left him needing jaw surgery.

However, Martinez is now back in the picture to put the pressure back on Mike Penders, who made up for a dodgy debut against Tottenham Hotspur with a hard-fought clean sheet against Manchester United last weekend.

As momentum is on Penders's side, Xabi Alonso may feel that he can err on the side of caution with Martinez, and the former has our vote to hold his spot in between the sticks.

Penders should be shielded by an unchanged backline in Josh Acheampong, Wesley Fofana, Levi Colwill and Marco Palestra, as Maxence Lacroix, Reece James and Jorrel Hato are all still unavailable.

Alonso may be forced into a midfield alteration, though, as Moises Caicedo is suffering from discomfort, so Jordan Henderson - fully fit again after an illness - could join forces with Romeo Lavia.

Left out of Thomas Tuchel's England squad once more, all eyes will be on Cole Palmer, as the 24-year-old lines up with Estevao Willian, Pedro Neto and Morgan Rogers in another Joao Pedro-less attack.

Penders; Acheampong, Fofana, Colwill, Palestra; Henderson, Lavia; Estevao, Palmer, Rogers; Neto

#2013. Cisse says Milan ‘need to forget’ about derby win amid Europa League struggles

Alphadjo Cisse spoke to the media this evening and said that Milan need to forget about the derby win and build on the momentum with more wins.

The derby win certainly put Milan and the fans on cloud nine, especially since it wasn’t just a narrow 1-0 win. However, they now need to put some of that confidence to use in the Europa League as they only have three points after three games.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Ferencvaros are the opponents this evening, travelling to San Siro for the first time, and it could be a tough one as they are on nine points so far. Ruben Amorim clearly has faith in some of his deputies, though, with six changes made to the starting eleven.

Alphadjo Cisse is one of the players in the starting eleven and just a few minutes ago, he spoke to Sky Italia (via MilanNews) about the task at hand. He made it clear that Milan cannot keep thinking about the derby win, instead focusing on getting more wins.

“It’s important for me and the whole team. We always try to play to our full potential.”

“It was an important victory. But we need to forget about it and build on that momentum with a win. Getting the three points is important today.”

“I actually don’t know anything yet, the squad list hasn’t been released yet. I’d be very happy if the call were to come. But I’m thinking about today and tomorrow will be another day.”

#2011. ‘Matter of fact’ – Virgil van Dijk issues Liverpool reality check after defeat to Arsenal

Virgil van Dijk has advised Liverpool to forget about what their Premier League rivals are doing and concentrate on themselves, following the defeat to Arsenal at the weekend.

The Reds now trail the champions and leaders by nine points after the 1-0 loss at Anfield on Sunday, and Daily Mail writer Ian Ladyman said that the result shows that Andoni Iraola’s side are ‘not ready‘ to properly contend for the top-flight title this season.

It was a second home defeat in the space of a month for LFC, who were also beaten on their own patch by second-placed Manchester City, and the veteran Dutch defender acknowledged that his team are in a transitional phase after changing head coach over the summer.

Speaking to reporters after the defeat to Arsenal, Van Dijk proclaimed (via Liverpool Echo): “We have to just focus on ourselves.

“I don’t think it is good to think about the other two [Arsenal and Man City] and even [third-placed] Brighton. We have to focus on ourselves and we are in a process.

“We have been together now for four months but we play at Liverpool and we want results every three days, especially at home.

“The main thing is we keep working very hard and that we see improvement, but the matter of fact is we are in a transition. [Arsenal] was a great opportunity to get a good result, but unfortunately it didn’t happen, so we have to take it.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Nobody realistically expected Liverpool to challenge for the title at the start of the season, so it wouldn’t be a failure if the Reds aren’t in contention for the trophy by the time April rolls around.

The objective for this campaign was to finish closer to the summit and show discernible improvement on a wretched 2025/26, and recent performances suggest that Iraola is capable of delivering in that regard.

His team are currently on course to end the season with 63 points (just three more than last term), but if they improve on a home record of just one win from five league games so far, they should be able to nudge that projected total into the 70s.

Liverpool competed admirably with Arsenal and Man City (up until the harsh red card for Ryan Gravenberch) but weren’t as clinical as the top two in those games. With more ruthlessness in attack, the Reds seem capable of at least closing that gap.

Van Dijk is correct – the goal for this season isn’t to compete for the title, but to qualify for the Champions League with relative comfort and lay the foundations for further improvement in 2027/28.

There’s still plenty of room for improvement, but at least there are signs of this campaign being much more convincing than 2025/26 had been.

#2010. Rangers handed ‘season-defining’ Celtic title race boost

Barry Ferguson believes Rangers’ Premier Sports Cup semi-final victory over Aberdeen could prove to be a “season-defining moment” for Derek McInnes and his players.

Ryan Naderi struck the winner at Hampden to book Rangers a place in next month’s final against Hibs, with Ferguson admitting he could feel the tension building as the game remained goalless.

The former Ibrox captain believes defeat would have brought intense scrutiny on McInnes and his new-look squad, but was impressed by the way they handled the pressure.

Writing in his Daily Record column, Ferguson said: “Make no mistake, what happened at the weekend might be looked upon as a season-defining moment.

“Had Aberdeen nicked it then everything Derek is working so hard to put in place would have been rocked from the ground up.”

Ferguson feels Rangers demonstrated a mentality reminiscent of successful Ibrox sides by refusing to panic as the prospect of extra time loomed.

Celtic star makes ‘terrified’ opposition claim after spearheading comeback

Derek McInnes delivers 'unbelievable' verdict on unsung Rangers standout

Vaclav Cerny nightmare as Celtic mission flops and Rangers hero lands transfer fear

“They stood up to the situation and found a way of getting through it,” he said. “And that’s the stuff that successful Rangers teams have always been made of.

“There’s still work to do. But, week by week, challenge by challenge Del and his team are getting there.”

Rangers then received another boost when Celtic suffered a 2-0 Premiership defeat at Falkirk the following day.

The result has given McInnes’ side an opportunity to crank up the pressure in the title race, with Ferguson adamant Rangers must now address their recent problems away from Ibrox.

He added: “Rangers are back breathing down their necks. Or at least they will be if they can win at St Mirren on Saturday night to cut the gap to just a single point.”

Ferguson believes victory in Paisley would allow Rangers to apply further pressure before Celtic host Kilmarnock, but warned that the cup final cannot become a distraction.

“They have given themselves a shot at the first silverware of the season, and that’s great,” he said. “But now they have to send out a message that they won’t be satisfied with lifting just one trophy between now and May.”

#2009. ‘It affected my family’ – VAR official reveals full impact of huge decision which cost Liverpool

The official who was on VAR duty for the wrongly disallowed Luis Diaz goal in Liverpool’s 2-1 defeat to Tottenham in 2023 has spoken about the impact that the controversy had on his family.

The Colombian thought he had put the Reds 1-0 up in the 35th minute of the game in north London, but he was incorrectly flagged for offside, and a subsequent review from Stockley Park saw that erroneous decision upheld.

When the audio from the VAR conversation was publicly released a few days later, it was revealed that Darren England – the official on duty – had given the message of ‘check complete’ to the on-field referee in the mistaken belief that the goal was allowed to stand.

The 40-year-old has given an interview to BBC Sport in which he reflected on the regret from that hugely controversial decision, and how the fallout seeped into his family life.

England recalled: “Once I realised I’d made the error, it’s a really difficult place to try to forget that and move on. I can’t just physically stand up and walk out and leave it alone. A lot of resilience was needed – a lot of experience as well.”

He added: “The aftermath obviously was really difficult to deal with. It was challenging because it’s the goldfish bowl of the Premier League, but when mistakes happen, then you’re in the public eye and criticism’s inevitably going to come your way.

“That was difficult because it affected my family as well. We had people outside my girls’ school, journalists and things like that. That then affects you not as a referee, but as a human being.”

The catalogue of errors which led to Diaz’s legitimate goal being disallowed was farcical, with all of the officials on duty collectively culpable for the shambolic process which unfolded.

England did acknowledge in the VAR audio that he thought the on-field decision was onside and immediately held his hands up to the error, but that came as no comfort to anyone associated with Liverpool after such a costly and preventable outcome.

🚨 OFFICIAL: PGMOL have released VAR audio from Spurs v Liverpool 🔊 pic.twitter.com/zNLDyHkBbe

— Football on TNT Sports (@footballontnt) October 3, 2023

Criticism of the officials botching the process was inevitable and justified, but obviously the media intrusion into the referee’s family life crossed an unacceptable line, and we can empathise with how difficult the fallout must’ve been for the now 40-year-old.

Unfortunately, more than three years on from that chaotic blunder, refereeing standards in the Premier League haven’t improved to any great extent, as we saw at the weekend with the inexplicable decision not to award a penalty for a clear pull by Jurrien Timber on Alexander Isak’s shirt.

Pro Ref chief executive Howard Webb needs to do much more to ensure that a satisfactory standard of officiating is reached, but no person deserves to have an error in the course of the work turn into an unwarranted invasion on their family life.

#2006. Celtic vs Kilmarnock - prediction, team news, lineups

By Calum Burrowes | 06 Nov 2026 15:05, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 20:38

Looking to move seven points clear at the top of the Scottish Premiership, Celtic return to league action on Sunday when they welcome Kilmarnock to Glasgow for their second meeting this season.

The Bhoys secured a dramatic second-half comeback victory over Besiktas in the Europa League during the week, while Killie head into this encounter on the back of a 2-2 draw with St Johnstone on Halloween.

After drawing with Dundee United and suffering their first defeat to Falkirk in nearly two decades, Martin O'Neill and his Celtic side went into their midweek clash with Turkish giants Besiktas in desperate need of a positive result, having dropped to second-bottom in the Europa League league-phase table.

The Bhoys produced a lacklustre first-half display at Celtic Park on Thursday night, managing just two touches in the opposition box during the opening 45 minutes. When they fell 1-0 behind shortly after the restart, it looked as though the Glasgow giants were heading for another disappointing European result.

However, substitutes Callum Osmand and Camilo Duran inspired a remarkable turnaround as Celtic took the lead, were pegged back in the 85th minute and then responded once again to secure a 3-2 victory over Vincenzo Italiano's side.

The three points provided a much-needed boost for O'Neill's men, whose lead at the top of the Scottish Premiership had been cut after collecting just one point from their previous two league outings.

Despite the demanding nature of their European comeback, the result could provide the confidence needed to spark an improvement in domestic performances.

Celtic currently hold a four-point advantage at the summit, although arch-rivals Rangers have a game in hand and could move above them if the Bhoys fail to return to winning ways on Sunday.

As for Kilmarnock, they travel to Glasgow seeking their first victory over Celtic since December 2023, having failed to win any of their previous 10 meetings with the Scottish champions.

Having finished third-bottom last season, Kilmarnock avoided the relegation playoffs with four consecutive victories to close out the 2025-26 campaign, but they would have been hoping to build on that strong finish rather than find themselves battling near the foot of the table again.

Under Neil McCann, who has won 36% of his matches since taking charge in January 2026, Kilmarnock have struggled for consistency and currently sit 11th in the 12-team division.

Two wins, three draws and seven defeats from their opening 12 matches have left McCann's side with just nine points, highlighting several areas that need to improve sooner rather than later.

Defensive frailties have been a particular concern, with Killie already conceding 28 goals at an average of 2.3 per game.

That is comfortably the worst defensive record in the Scottish Premiership, with second-highest Motherwell and St Mirren having shipped 20.

Celtic emerged from their European victory without any further injury concerns, although changes are likely after Duran and Osmand made an impact from the bench, with the former scoring twice and the latter also finding the net.

James Forrest and Sebastian Tounekti could be the players to make way, allowing both substitutes to earn starting roles.

Canadian full-back Alistair Johnston and Yang Hyun-Jun remain sidelined through injury, although both are expected to return in the coming weeks.

As for the visitors, McCann could stick with the same starting XI that drew 2-2 with 10-man St Johnstone as he looks to find some much-needed consistency.

Former Manchester United academy product Joe Hugill is expected to retain his place up front as he looks to build on the four goal involvements he has recorded this season.

McCann will be without Bailey Rice and Maksymillian Stryjek.

Johnstone; Lotomba, Carter-Vickers, Scales, Tierney; Nygren, McGregor, Baur; Duran, Hogh, Osmand

Manti; McCarthy, Deas, Stanger; Brandon, Tshibola, Lowery, Ring; Kiltie; Hugill, Daniels

Although Celtic have been inconsistent in recent weeks, their comeback victory over Besiktas should provide a timely confidence boost, and we expect them to return to winning ways in the league on Sunday.

Kilmarnock have looked particularly vulnerable defensively this season, and we believe the hosts will have enough attacking quality to exploit those weaknesses and secure a comfortable 3-0 victory.

#2005. After 18 months away, I’ve finally got my Scotland chance again

Former Hibernian defender Ryan Porteous has been handed a Scotland recall after Stephen Welsh was forced to withdraw through injury.

Porteous has been drafted into Sebastien Pocognoli’s squad for the upcoming Nations League fixtures against North Macedonia and Switzerland.

The centre-back has endured a difficult spell at international level since his red card in Scotland’s 5-1 defeat by Germany in the opening match of Euro 2024.

The former Easter Road favourite has made just one Scotland appearance since then, featuring in the Nations League play-off against Greece in March.

But Porteous has continued to push for an international return, and his form across the Atlantic has now earned him another opportunity.

The 27-year-old has been a regular for Los Angeles FC in MLS this season, starting 25 of their 33 league fixtures.

(Image: Will G MacNeil/Los Angeles FC/Getty Images)

His Scotland return comes after Welsh suffered an injury while on club duty with Swansea City. The former Celtic and Motherwell defender’s problem is not thought to be serious, but it will keep him out of the forthcoming double-header.

Porteous had recently admitted that getting back into the Scotland squad remained a driving force following the disappointment of the Euros.

“It was always going to be difficult after the Euros,” he said.

“But after the first few months of maybe feeling sorry for myself a little bit, every training session, every gym session, every game, has always been, how can I get back into that squad?

“How can I force my way back into that squad?

“It’s always my goal. It’s always my drive to play for Scotland because it’s the pinnacle and there’s no better feeling in football.”

The latest call-up now gives the former Hibs defender the opportunity he has been craving as Scotland prepare to face North Macedonia and Switzerland.

#2000. Liverpool's £123m Bradley Barcola problem: Iraola under scrutiny

By Naim Beneddra | 06 Nov 2026 15:17

Bradley Barcola's difficult start at Liverpool has raised questions about whether Andoni Iraola is making the best use of the French winger, with the manager himself acknowledging a significant difference in the player's performances depending on his position.

The 24-year-old arrived from Paris Saint-Germain in August in a deal worth up to £123m, but has struggled to reproduce the consistency that made him one of Europe's most exciting attacking talents.

His three Liverpool goals have all come in the same Champions League match against LASK, while he has contributed two assists in the Premier League. Thirteen appearances into his Anfield career, the return remains modest given the expectations surrounding his arrival.

However, Barcola's struggles cannot be explained by his finishing alone. He has featured in several attacking roles under Iraola, including an unfamiliar central position during Wednesday's 3-2 Champions League defeat to Fenerbahce.

The Spanish coach's subsequent assessment has brought a wider tactical question into focus: why has Liverpool's expensive summer signing spent so much time away from the position in which he is most effective?

Iraola's decision to deploy Barcola as a central striker in Istanbul was partly influenced by the availability of his other attacking players.

With Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz starting on the wings, Alexander Isak was initially kept on the bench, having been earmarked for a shorter appearance.

Liverpool's manager believed Barcola's acceleration could cause problems for Fenerbahce's defenders, particularly when attacking the space behind their back line.

"We thought it would work well because I think Bradley, in terms of speed and the match-ups, it could be good for him," Iraola explained after the defeat.

However, he acknowledged that the experiment had not produced the same attacking threat as some of Liverpool's more familiar combinations.

"All season he has been better when he has played outside wide," Iraola admitted.

The assessment was revealing, particularly given Barcola's preference for operating on the left.

Of his 13 Liverpool appearances, six have come away from that preferred position, including five on the right and Wednesday's experiment through the middle.

Barcola's greatest strengths are his acceleration, close control and ability to isolate defenders in one-on-one situations. On the left, he can receive the ball facing an opponent, accelerate into space and create opportunities with either a cutback or a direct run towards goal.

Operating centrally presents a different challenge.

Against teams defending with limited space between their centre-backs, he is required to receive more frequently with his back to goal, hold off defenders and make decisions in congested areas.

Those demands do not necessarily suit a player whose most dangerous actions often begin with a run from a wider position.

Iraola has not ruled out using him through the middle again, insisting that such an arrangement could be useful against particular opponents.

Nevertheless, Liverpool's attacking performance in Istanbul offered little evidence that it should become his regular role.

Isak scored after replacing Ngumoha in the second half, while the Reds were more threatening once they had greater presence in central areas.

Barcola has also been guilty of individual errors that cannot be attributed to his positioning.

Against Brentford, for example, he attempted an unsuccessful chip when through on goal and later lost possession after delaying a pass during a promising counter-attack.

His decision-making and finishing therefore remain legitimate areas for improvement, regardless of where Iraola selects him.

There are mitigating circumstances surrounding Barcola's arrival that help explain his uneven performances.

Liverpool agreed to pay PSG an initial £106m, with a further £17m in potential add-ons, making the Frenchman one of the most expensive signings in the club's history.

Yet the transfer was completed only towards the end of August, depriving him of a full pre-season with Iraola and his new teammates.

Barcola had also been involved in the World Cup during the summer, leaving him with limited preparation before adapting to a different league and a new tactical environment.

His first Liverpool appearance came in early September, following several weeks without competitive football.

The physical demands of the Premier League have presented another adjustment, while Liverpool's difficulties against compact defensive teams have not always allowed Barcola to exploit the space that made him so effective at PSG.

There is also the challenge of developing an understanding with teammates who are themselves adapting to Iraola's methods.

In an exclusive interview with Sky Sports, published before the Fenerbahce defeat, Barcola acknowledged that he had yet to reach his best level.

"No, I don't think I'm at my best yet," he admitted. "You still haven't seen the best version of me."

The Frenchman believes improving his relationship with those around him will be crucial.

"On top of that, we're working with my team-mates so that they can make the most of my strengths," he explained.

"So yes, I think once we really develop that understanding, things will get much better."

Barcola's comments suggest that he recognises the need to improve without regarding his difficult start as evidence that the transfer has failed.

Nor does he consider his fee or the responsibility of succeeding Mohamed Salah to be an additional burden, insisting that he wants to establish his own identity at Anfield.

The challenge for Iraola is to find an attacking structure that helps him do so.

Ngumoha and Munoz have provided encouraging alternatives on the flanks, while Isak and Cody Gakpo offer different qualities through the middle. Those options give the Liverpool manager flexibility, but also complicate the task of establishing a settled role for Barcola.

The Reds travel to Crystal Palace on Sunday, when Iraola will have another opportunity to reconsider his attacking selection following the defeat in Turkey.

Barcola must improve his finishing and decision-making if he is to justify Liverpool's investment. But with his manager openly acknowledging that he performs better out wide, how consistently he is allowed to operate in that position will be an important part of assessing his progress.

#1999. AC Milan 0-2 Ferencvaros: Rossoneri fall to another dire Europa League defeat

AC Milan fell to a third Europa League defeat in four games as they were beaten 2-0 at home by Ferencvaros.

The hero of the night for the Hungarian side was without doubt Lenny Joseph, who netted twice in the second half to capitalise firstly on a loose touch from Lorenzo Torriani and then from a two-on-one break.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

A red card for the substitute Yusif threatened to change the momentum of the game, but the Rossoneri were unable to fashion any real response to put the result in doubt in what was another forgettable European night.

The result means that Milan have now dropped out of even the top 24 spots, and they can just about say goodbye to any hopes of direct last-16 qualification barring a miracle.

Ruben Amorim chose to make six changes from the team that beat Inter in the derby, with Lorenzo Torriani, Filippo Terracciano, Davide Bartesaghi, Ardon Jashari, Omari Hutchinson and Alphadjo Cisse coming into the team.

Ferencvaros started the game on top and they created the first big chance of the game less than four minutes in. A loose pass as Milan tried to build out was seized upon by Zachariassen who threaded Joseph through, and though his initial attempt was blocked by Koni De Winter, the forward managed to get another shot off from a few yards out that was thankfully straight at Torriani.

The first 15 minutes were quite frankly dreadful from Milan, in complete contrast to the victory at the weekend. The away side dominated possession thanks to so many sloppy giveaways, and Birmancevic nearly found himself bearing down on goal in a central area though he fired at his own man after some good close control.

It continued to be all the Hungarian side as the majority of the San Siro crowd began to grow worried and impatient. Another shot towards the goal came in the 17th minute, and even if Zachariassen did roll it straight at Torriani the fact he was found in space beyond the defensive line caused more worry.

Milan did not grow into the game as hoped and the errors kept coming. A stray pass backwards from Jashari under pressure put Joseph through on goal for Ferencvaros, though Torriani read his shot towards the bottom right corner well and was able to claim it. Another warning sign, however.

The first half was probably best summarised by two fouls in quick succession. The first saw Cisse act on the frustration of losing the ball and go lunging in to earn a yellow card that in fairness to the youngster was harsh, then Bartesaghi lost possession near the touchline before clumsily bundling his man over to give away a free-kick.

It took until the 39th minute for Milan to have their first shot of the game, but Cisse lashed it well over the bar from an Adrien Rabiot knock-down that landed nicely just beyond the penalty spot. At the other end, Joseph got the better of Diawara to surge into the box, yet Torriani was equal to his effort from a very narrow angle.

Torriani was by far the busier of the two goalkeepers and he was called into action again a few minutes from the break, with Joseph again the man who found space to shoot inside the box. The Italian got a strong hand to thwart the angled drive.

Amorim was clearly very displeased with what he saw in the first half, as he chose to make three changes at the break, bringing on Mario Gila, Diego Moreira and Christian Pulisic. Diawara, Cisse and Yunus Musah were the ones to come off.

Milan started the second half the better of the two sides, with Hutchinson firing into the side netting and then Ramos going on a winding run past three players into the box before a deflected shot.

Seven minutes into the second half, the deadlock was finally broken and it was unfortunately a moment to forget for Torriani. De Winter played a bit of a demanding pass back to the goalkeeper inside the box and the heavy first touch was seized upon, with the Ferencvaros player going down for what would have been a penalty had Joseph not been on hand to slot into an empty net.

The Rossoneri’s response was almost instant with Ramos again at the centre of some good work on the edge of the box, feeding Hutchinson’s run beyond the last man down the left side of the box, though the shot across goal just rolled wide of the far post.

In the 66th minute, Ferencvaros dealt Milan a sucker punch as they doubled their advantage just after Jashari had come off for Luka Modric. A bit of a ricochet in midfield led to a dangerous two-on-one situation for the visitors, allowing Zachariassen to lay it on a plate to Joseph, who simply had to slot it into an empty net.

The final change came just after with Francesco Camarda coming on for Bartesaghi, and he was not far from reopening the contest with a near-post flick from Moreira’s cross. Up the other end, a quickly taken free-kick saw Zachariassen’s half-volley draw a reaction save from Torriani.

There was a moment of madness from the substitute Yusuf with 15 minutes left on the clock as he seemed to reach out an elbow to strike Gila unprovoked. The Spaniard went down, VAR took a look and the referee sent him off.

Dibusz hadn’t been very busy all night, but the veteran goalkeeper was called upon to make a good save with his legs from Hutchinson’s shot through a crowd. It was looking more and more like not being the Diavolo’s night.

Ferencvaros should have had a third in the second of four added minutes when another loose pass towards Torriani was collected by Madarasz, who rounded the keeper but hit the side-netting.

#1998. England squad controversy: Thomas Tuchel explains Cole Palmer absence as "desperate" Premier League star ahead of Chelsea man

By Lewis Nolan | 06 Nov 2026 15:18

England boss Thomas Tuchel has revealed that Cole Palmer has been left out of his squad for the November international break because he has missed too many chances to impress.

Premier League football will pause after this weekend so that Nations League fixtures can take place, and the Three Lions have named their 25-man squad.

Chelsea attacker Palmer has once again been left out by Tuchel, though he has called up Fulham forward Josh King, who plays in a similar position.

Speaking to reporters, Tuchel argued that Palmer has often missed the chance to impress, saying: "We have enough number 10s and we stick to the guys who were in the previous camp because we were happy with the two and a half weeks we had together.

"We have Josh King as a new player in there, but I want to see him on both wings. He is kind of an extra player and he can play all four positions. I guess everyone is desperate to play for England and Cole is no exception.

"We are speaking now about a player that is not in camp. It counts when you are in camp and I just said last time that he misses too many opportunities to impress."

Palmer was left out of England's squad for their games in early autumn, and he will play no part against either Croatia on November 12 or Spain on November 15.

Palmer has undoubtedly proven more at the top level of football than the likes of Morgan Gibbs-White and King, with the attacker even scoring in the Euro 2024 final.

However, the Englishman has been disappointing for Chelsea for some time, especially when playing against the division's best teams.

The 24-year-old has registered just five goal involvements in his last 19 league appearances against the Premier League's big six.

It should also be noted that Palmer has scored just four non-penalty goals in his last 26 games for Chelsea, and given his poor performance levels, he cannot be surprised to have been left out of the England squad.

King has been in exceptional form for Fulham this season, with the attacker playing out wide on the right and in a more central role.

The 19-year-old has scored once and assisted twice despite the struggles of his team, and his confidence will have been boosted thanks to Tuchel's decision to include him in his squad.

Exactly the same can be said for winger Rio Ngumoha, who was selected by Tuchel to play in England's friendlies prior to the World Cup, and becoming accustomed to the national team now could bode well for their chances of playing at Euro 2028.

#1997. ‘Painful’ – Alexis Mac Allister doesn’t hold back about ‘unpleasant situation’ at Liverpool

Alexis Mac Allister has spoken out about his ‘painful, unpleasant situation’ at Liverpool in terms of not being offered a new contract.

The Argentine caused a stir in September when he said that he was ‘very sad‘ not to have been offered a new deal by the club, having seen fellow 2023 signings Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai both pen contract extensions earlier this year.

The Telegraph’s Dominic King reported last month that Anfield chiefs aren’t in ‘any rush’ to begin talks over a new deal for the Reds’ number 10 (who’s contracted to June 2028), despite his resurgence in form since the start of this season.

Appearing on the Los Edul show in his homeland, Mac Allister spoke candidly about Liverpool’s decision not to offer him new terms over the past few months.

The 27-year-old said: “We’re in a situation where I have a year and a half left on my contract. Last season I was told that the club’s idea was not to renew it, at least for now, and obviously that was a painful, unpleasant situation.”

When asked if the situation was making him despondent, he replied: “Not that much, because at the end of the day, I still had – and still have – time left at this club, which is what I want most – to stay here.

“The reality is that the manager has now changed, the sporting director has changed, and new investors are coming into the club, so I think I’m now in a position where anything can happen. We’ll see what happens in the future. I’ve always said that I’m very happy here, that I really enjoy it, and we’ll see.”

Mac Allister added: “Look at Szoboszlai and Gravenberch. They’re two players who were in the same contractual situation as me, and when I was told that, they renewed their contracts.

“It was more a position taken by the club, and generally that’s how things are done. At the end of the day, as a club you don’t want to lose a lot of money, and you don’t want players leaving on free transfers either.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

That the Argentine has spoken out publicly about his contract situation once more gives a strong hint that privately he’s seething at not being offered a new deal in the same way that Szoboszlai and Gravenberch were.

Admittedly Mac Allister’s collapse in form last season may have triggered a reluctance from the club to commit to a contract extension for a player who’ll be 29 when his current terms expire, and he’s a bit older than his aforementioned midfield teammates.

However, the ex-Brighton man has been excellent in the first two months of this campaign, almost as though he’s motivated by a burning desire to earn a new deal at Anfield and show that the hierarchy have been mistaken in their reluctance to tie him down for the long-term.

The 2022 World Cup winner is currently on £180,000 per week at Liverpool, a figure exceeded by 10 of his teammates (Capology), and it could be the case that he’s seeking a higher amount than what the club are prepared to offer him.

Mac Allister could hardly have made his desire for a new contract any clearer. We don’t know exactly why his situation is taking longer to resolve than those of Szoboszlai and Gravenberch, but if he keeps performing on the pitch, then surely it’s just a matter of when and not if he’s offered an extension by the Anfield hierarchy.

#1996. Napoli vs Lazio - prediction, team news, lineups

By Jonathan O'Shea | 06 Nov 2026 15:25, Last updated: 08 Nov 2026 08:54

Trending in very different directions, Serie A leaders Lazio will visit a faltering Napoli side on Sunday, as Stadio Maradona hosts the lunchtime kickoff.

While the home side are struggling both in Europe and Italy's top flight, their southern rivals have posted nine wins from 10 and are yet to taste defeat in the league.

Sparking crisis talks between the coaching staff and club president Aurelio Di Laurentiis, Napoli are in danger of missing this season's objectives with several months left to play.

On Wednesday night, the Partenopei suffered a chastening 4-1 defeat to Porto, meaning they have lost seven of their last eight Champions League away games. Having finished 30th in the 36-team table last term, they currently sit 27th - inside the elimination zone.

A former finalist with Juventus, head coach Massimiliano Allegri has personally lost nine of his last 11 matches at Europe's elite level, and he is also under pressure for some dire domestic results.

Napoli lie eighth in Serie A after last week's 2-0 defeat to Juve, and with a 14-point deficit to surprise leaders Lazio they are surely out of the title race.

Defeat this weekend would result in their worst start since 2007, and Allegri cannot expect any favours from his former midfield general at AC Milan.

While Gennaro Gattuso has lost all five of their meetings in management, recent events suggest that trend could soon end.

Including a frantic 3-3 draw in the Derby del Sole, Napoli have gone six games without a clean sheet while conceding 13 goals, and they must now host Roma's fierce city rivals.

Precedent is certainly on Lazio's side, having won on all of their last four visits to Naples and prevailed in five of the last eight meetings overall.

More pertinently, the capital club have just won six consecutive Serie A games, leaving their more optimistic fans dreaming of a first Scudetto since the 1999-2000 campaign.

Gattuso will not be drawn on such talk, even though his side boast the division's joint-best defensive record and have scored at least twice in their last eight matches.

This century, only four teams have previously hit 28 points after 10 matchdays, and that tally has lifted them three clear of reigning champions Inter Milan.

Along the way, Lazio have also had 12 different goalscorers, with Gustav Isaksen finding the net four times in his last five appearances.

The Danish winger was on target in last week's 2-1 win over Cagliari, as the Biancocelesti capitalised on Inter's Milan derby defeat and took sole possession of top spot.

Now, Gattuso will return to a club where he won the Coppa Italia but was subsequently sacked, seeking an incredible sixth straight away win in Serie A.

Adding to the sense of crisis in Naples, Allegri has been hampered by a long injury list for several weeks.

Alessandro Buongiorno, David Neres, Costantino Favasuli, Alisson Santos, Leonardo Spinazzola, Benoit Badiashile and Stanislav Lobotka are all unavailable.

Furthermore, captain Giovanni Di Lorenzo sustained a muscular injury last weekend, when Luca Marianucci was sent off against Juventus and incurred a one-match ban.

Despite his advancing years and chequered fitness history, Kevin De Bruyne may be asked to go again, having scored three goals in his last five league games.

Without Europe to consider, Gattuso has made relatively few changes so far, and it should be a settled Lazio side that takes to the field on Sunday.

However, he will have to replace captain Mattia Zaccagni, who could be ruled out until next month with a thigh strain.

Albert Gudmundsson is still sidelined after dislocating his shoulder on Iceland duty, but with Adam Marusic and Nicolo Rovella finally back in full training, everyone else should be available.

Meret; Beukema, Rrahmani, Marin; Politano, Anguissa, De Bruyne, McTominay, Olivera; Vergara; Hojlund

Mandas; Floriani Mussolini, Sutalo, Provstgaard, Tavares; Frattesi, Belahyane, Taylor; Isaksen, Pinamonti, Noslin

Struggling in Serie A, facing another early exit from Europe and burdened by a huge absence list, Napoli are set to lose three games on the spin.

While Lazio's stellar run will surely end soon, they can exploit their hosts' shaky defence and post a seventh straight win.

#1994. FC Twente vs Ajax - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adepoju Marvellous | 06 Nov 2026 16:02

The standout fixture of gameweek 12 in the 2026-27 Eredivisie campaign sees FC Twente and Ajax face off at De Grolsch Veste.

Both teams begin Sunday’s heavyweight clash inside the top four, with the possibility that one could finish the weekend at the summit.

Just four days after recording their biggest-ever league win away at SBV Excelsior in a 9-0 thrashing, Twente faced a more demanding continental test against Pafos on Thursday, coming from behind to claim a 3-1 victory in their third Conference League outing.

One of three teams still boasting a perfect record in Europe’s third-tier competition, Trots van het Oosten are in pole position to reach the knockout stages of a UEFA tournament for the first time since 2011, continuing to make waves in their first full season under John van den Brom.

Riding their joint-longest winning run in over three years, Twente now face arguably their toughest test of the campaign so far. Emerging unscathed would only intensify the growing whispers of a potential title challenge.

The Tukkers have beaten this weekend’s opponent just once in the last five meetings, though that victory came in the most recent clash back in April, when Ramiz Zerrouki and Bart van Rooy netted to seal a 2-1 win.

With only 10 goals conceded - the fewest in the division - a newfound defensive solidity has underpinned Twente’s success so far. It also helps that they have been quick starters, scoring first in eight of their last nine league outings.

Ajax were also in Conference League action in midweek, running riot against Danish side Midtjylland with a 6-1 thrashing at the MCH Arena, picking up where they left off in their last league outing against AZ Alkmaar.

That marked a fifth consecutive victory, as Michel’s men have wasted no time in bouncing back from a three-match winless run either side of the September/October international break - a spell that threatened to derail their ambitions for the season.

Currently the only Eredivisie side with a perfect away record, De Godenzonen now head to Enschede aiming to stay within touching distance of leaders Feyenoord, who could be five points clear by the time proceedings get underway in Twente.

Up against the league’s top scorer, Wout Weghorst, and the leading assist provider, Sondre Orjasaeter, Ajax have their work cut out in their quest for consecutive victories at De Grolsch Veste for the first time since 2021.

Like their hosts, Sunday’s visitors have delivered the first blow more often than not lately - breaking the deadlock in each of their last five outings - and will hope it continues in a fixture whose last six editions have seen them concede the opener five times.

Stav Lemkin (muscle) has yet to feature for Twente this season and is ruled out on Sunday, alongside fellow defender Max Bruns.

First-choice goalkeeper Lars Unnerstall remains sidelined, so Joel Drommel should make a ninth consecutive start between the sticks.

Twenty-year-old Filip Thorvaldsen has endured an injury-hit debut campaign and is once again out of contention for the hosts.

Ajax are contending with a lengthy injury list, with up to eight players potentially missing this weekend’s clash.

Caio Henrique and Anton Gaaei are significant absentees at the back, while the loss of Sofyan Amrabat and Julian Brandt further limits Ajax’s midfield options.

Viktor Tsygankov, Simon Adingra, Kasper Dolberg, and Oliver Valaker Edvardsen remain unavailable in attack, meaning leading scorer Tolu Arokodare is unlikely to be rested after his brace against Midtjylland.

Drommel; Van Rooy, Propper, Nijstad, Adelgaard; Zerrouki, Weidmann; Rots, Taha, Orjasaeter; Weghorst

Ter Stegen; Wijndal, Janse, Bouwman, Rosa; Baas, Mokio; Gloukh, Klaassen, Ouazane; Arokodare

Given the strong form of both sides, Sunday’s clash could go either way and is difficult to call.

As a result, we are leaning towards a share of the spoils, with honours even at the full-time whistle.

#1993. Player Ratings: AC Milan 0-2 Ferencvaros – Torriani howler; several struggle

AC Milan failed to revive their Europa League campaign, losing 2-0 at home to Ferencvaros. Several players failed to perform and below are the ratings for the Rossoneri.

After a mere three points in three games, Milan headed into the clash knowing that a win was more or less a must. Sadly, that didn’t show on the pitch as Ferencvaros deservedly got all of the glory, with the Rossoneri struggling on many fronts.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

If you haven’t already, make sure to check out how we decide the player ratings. From the scale to what affects the rating, we have compiled everything there.

👎 Torriani (4.5): It wasn’t the kindest of backpasses just before the first goal, but man, he needed to do so much better with the first touch. Heavy with all caps would be the way to describe it. In fairness to him, he couldn’t do anything about the first goal and made several good stops throughout.

👔 Amorim (4): In my opinion, this was more of a tactical failure rather than individuals letting Milan down. Ferencvaros had full control of the game and not even bringing on the big guns helped the gaffer. We all warned that the rotation perhaps wasn’t the best idea either.

Torriani (4.5): It wasn’t the kindest of backpasses just before the first goal, but man, he needed to do so much better with the first touch. Heavy with all caps would be the way to describe it. In fairness to him, he couldn’t do anything about the first goal and made several good stops throughout.

Terracciano (5): Was he the difference between a win and a defeat? Absolutely not, but also showed (once again) that he’s just not good enough. Poor defending on several occasions, cheap tricks that many referees would punish, and a general insecurity in possession. The cross attempt in the second half says it all.

De Winter (5.5): That backpass for Torriani should never be played in that way, even if Maignan is between the sticks. He admittedly got a bit unlucky with his clearance in the second half, but even then perhaps he could have done better. Anyway, for me it’s the pass which brings his rating down.

Diawara (5.5): He got beaten a few times at the back, but there weren’t any fatal errors and there were also a couple of good moments. However, overall, I would say it was just below an average display by him.

Bartesaghi (5): He knows how to run on the left flank, that’s for sure, but more often than not he doesn’t really get to the ball even if the pass is good. Also struggled a bit in possession tonight. One sequence was very telling when he tried to shield the ball and lost out completely instead.

Hutchinson (5): Awfully quiet in the first half and when he did get going in the second, there wasn’t much end product to his game. One good save denied him a goal, but he also missed a very good chance and didn’t have any luck with his crosses, really.,

Musah (5): There was one really poor giveaway at the start of the first half, in a proper Musah-esque way, and it probably should have resulted in a goal. Nothing about the rest of his performance was convincing either.

Jashari (5): Just like Musah, he nearly gifted a goal with a huge giveaway in the first half and it wasn’t a surprise to see him come off in the second half. The long balls didn’t have much accuracy and he struggled with Ferencvaros’ pressing.

Cisse (5.5): Milan didn’t really attack much in the first half, so that didn’t help him at all. However, even when he did end up in possession, I don’t think he was that good.

Rabiot (5): Given he wore the captain’s armband tonight and arguably is one of Milan’s best players, this was way below what we can demand from him. No luck in attack, both in terms of passes and finishes, and he also lost the ball a few times when the away side pressed high.

Ramos (5): The €74m man continues to struggle. There were some positive glimpses tonight and you cannot single him out as the worst player on the pitch, but he still needs to do so much more in his role.

Gila (5): He was way too rash just before the second goal, which opened up all the space even if Ferencvaros got a bit lucky. Before that, he had a poor giveaway and also had one right at the end, playing a weak pass to Torriani.

Moreira (6): As expected, the Belgian added energy to the game and also had some success on that right flank, sending several dangerous crosses into the box.

Pulisic (6): Just like Moreira, there was a noticeable difference as Milan were able to keep hold of the ball in the final third for much longer. However, the tactics probably let him and Moreira down in terms of actually being able to do something.

Modric (6): It didn’t take long for him to show that he remains fresh even at that age with a sprint to take control of the ball, and the rest was solid.

Amorim (4): In my opinion, this was more of a tactical failure rather than individuals letting Milan down. Ferencvaros had full control of the game and not even bringing on the big guns helped the gaffer. We all warned that the rotation perhaps wasn’t the best idea either.

#1992. Man United transfer news: Michael Carrick faces 'exciting' £23m battle with Chelsea and Arsenal for midfielder

By Lewis Nolan | 06 Nov 2026 16:14

Manchester United will have to battle the likes of Arsenal and Chelsea for Galatasaray midfielder Aleksey Batrakov, the latest report has claimed.

The Red Devils are readying themselves for their final game before the start of the November international break, with the club set to welcome Aston Villa to Old Trafford on Sunday.

A defeat could leave the team in the Premier League's relegation zone, and that would almost certainly lead to the dismissal of Michael Carrick.

United's struggles this campaign can in part be explained by the fact their midfield has performed poorly all season, including newcomer Carlos Baleba, who is now set for a period on the sidelines due to a hamstring injury.

It should come as no surprise to see the club linked to more midfielders, though TEAMtalk report that if United are to sign Galatasaray's Batrakov, they may have to convince the Russian to join them ahead of Arsenal and Chelsea.

Valued by Transfermarkt at just over £23m, Batrakov is unlikely to command a significant fee given he has never played in any of Europe's top five leagues.

The midfielder has performed excellently for Galatasaray, scoring five goals while providing three assists in 12 games for the club this season.

Four of those goals came in the Champions League, with the 21-year-old netting twice against Stuttgart, once against Lille and once against Barcelona.

Batrakov can play as either a number eight or an attacking midfielder, though he is arguably at his best when allowed to charge into the penalty area, so perhaps he could be seen as a replacement for Bruno Fernandes.

However, asking him to come to England and step into the void that could be left by the club's captain would be risky, and he should not be relied upon as a starter.

United should not be in a position where they need to sign yet another midfielder after signing three last summer.

It is alarming that co-owners INEOS, who reportedly have control over sporting decisions at Old Trafford, are seemingly admitting that their midfield revamp was a failure.

The Red Devils will also need to rebuild their defence over the next two transfer windows, while there are concerns about the level of their attack, so it remains to be seen if United will be able to fill the holes in their squad.

#1991. “I’m not Mo Salah” – Bradley Barcola speaks defiantly about his big-money Liverpool transfer

Bradley Barcola has said that he doesn’t feel any pressure to try and emulate Mo Salah at Liverpool and is instead focusing on creating his own legacy at Anfield.

At the end of the summer, the Reds spent an initial £106m (potentially rising to £123m, via The Athletic) to sign the French winger from Paris Saint-Germain, with the 24-year-old effectively brought in as the right-sided replacement for the Egyptian King.

It took the new signing seven matches to get off the mark for LFC, with that famine turning to feast in the form of a hat-trick against LASK in mid-October, and he’s followed that up with assists in the wins over Brentford and Brighton (Transfermarkt).

In an interview with Sky Sports, Barcola defiantly insisted that he doesn’t feel a burden to emulate Salah or repay the substantial transfer fee paid for him, with his sole focus being to make his ‘own mark’ and let his performances do the talking.

The France winger said: “First of all, I wasn’t the one who decided the transfer fee, so that’s not been my problem.

“Regarding Mo Salah, he’s a legend here, a huge one. He’s done big things here and, for that, I have an enormous respect for him, but it’s not pressure for me at all.

“I’m not Mo Salah, so I’m going to try to contribute whatever I can to the club and make my own mark on its history. I don’t feel any pressure about that.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Whoever was signed as the effective replacement for the legendary Egyptian was always going to face inevitable comparisons with our former no.11, but such were the standards set by Salah that striving to emulate him would be near-impossible.

Nobody is expecting Barcola to match the Trabzonspor man’s 257-goal tally for Liverpool over a nine-year period. As the Frenchman acknowledged, his job is simply to deliver the best that he can for the Reds.

There have been some moments to forget in his first few weeks on Merseyside, such as the missed sitter against Brentford last month, but he also conjured up a tremendous assist for Alexander Isak’s winning goal in the same match.

The 24-year-old might’ve drawn a blank against Arsenal on Sunday, but his direct running along the left flank was difficult for the Gunners to contain during the first half in particular, offering the kind of proactive threat that we love to see from wingers playing for LFC.

Salah was a unique figure at Liverpool, and Barcola doesn’t strictly have to emulate what the Egyptian has done in order to be regarded as a success at Anfield in time to come. We’ve seen glimpses of what he can offer to the Reds, and time is very much on his side to build upon that promising start.

#1990. Celtic ‘don’t have the legs’ as Chris Sutton unearths January transfer priority

Chris Sutton believes Celtic “don’t have the legs in midfield” to play Kasper Hogh and Camilo Duran together.

The former striker has questioned whether Martin O’Neill can find room for both centre-forwards in his current system, despite wanting to see the partnership given an opportunity.

Hogh endured another frustrating evening in the 3-2 Europa League win over Besiktas, while Duran came off the bench and struck twice to complete the comeback.

Sutton feels Hogh has suffered from a lack of service and believes the Dane could benefit from operating alongside Duran. Writing in his Daily Record column, Sutton said: “He’s struggling for decent service and I’d still like to see O’Neill finding a way to get him and Duran on the pitch at the same time.

The Celtic star who is 'absolute saviour' and teammate full of 'magic'

Celtic told ‘we’ll fight to win’ as Portuguese minnows dare to dream

Mika Baur gets Germany call-up after Celtic star misses senior cut

“We know why it can’t happen though, Celtic don’t have the legs in midfield to cope so it might be something that has to wait until that is addressed in the January transfer window.”

Sutton believes there can be little doubt over who should lead the line for Celtic. He added: “In the meantime Duran simply has to start. You could say the same about Osmand.”

Duran’s double against Besiktas strengthened his case for a regular central role, while Callum Osmand also made a major impact from the bench with a goal and an assist.

#1989. Inter Milan vs Como - prediction, team news, lineups

By Jonathan O'Shea | 06 Nov 2026 16:55, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 17:00

Having suffered derby defeat and slipped off top spot in Serie A, reigning champions Inter Milan must try to get back on track when they welcome record-breaking Como to San Siro on Sunday.

Following four intense meetings last term, the regional rivals are currently separated by two points, with both trailing surprise leaders Lazio.

Ending their 19-game undefeated streak in Serie A, Inter were well beaten by AC Milan in last week's Derby della Madonnina, making it eight straight second-city contests without a win.

With illness sweeping through Cristian Chivu's squad, those fit enough to start were swept aside by the rampant Rossoneri, who surged into an early two-goal lead and eventually won 3-1.

After falling three points behind Lazio, the Nerazzurri had little time to reflect and swiftly switched focus to their ailing European campaign.

Inter had claimed just three points from their opening three Champions League matches, but they were back near their best on Tuesday night, beating Feyenoord 3-0 at De Kuip.

Yann Bisseck put the visitors in front, and Pio Esposito doubled their lead before the break, with Piotr Zielinski adding an excellent third goal in the second half.

As a result, Chivu and co sit 14th in the table midway through this season's league phase, keeping them firmly in contention for the knockout rounds.

Before international football intervenes, they must now face a potential title rival - albeit one whom they have traditionally dominated.

History weighs heavily on Inter's side in this Lombardy derby, having won 14 consecutive Serie A home games against Como, while keeping a clean sheet in eight of the last nine.

Dating back down the decades, Como have lost their last 11 top-flight meetings with Inter, plus a recent Coppa Italia semi-final tie between the two sides.

Very much in demand, head coach Cesc Fabregas has come away empty-handed from each league game against a club that sought to appoint him in the summer of 2025.

Inter tried to lure the Catalan away from Como before hiring Chivu, but going toe-to-toe with the Nerazzurri has brought four straight Serie A defeats by a 12-3 aggregate scoreline.

That sequence includes a chastening 4-0 loss at San Siro last December, but the Biancoblu were unlucky not to reach the cup final after a thrilling semi-final second leg a few months later.

More recently, they have made Europe sit up and take notice with some eye-catching Champions League results, as the debutants followed their 4-1 defeat of Manchester United with a ruthless destruction of Lens.

Como travelled to France in midweek and left with an emphatic 9-1 victory, top scorer Tasos Douvikas helping himself to a hat-trick in an incredible rout.

That leaves the rookies above the likes of Barcelona, Bayern Munich and Inter in the table, with automatic entry to the last 16 now firmly fixed in their sights.

Since losing 3-2 to Feyenoord on matchday two, they have put together six consecutive wins across all competitions, scoring 22 goals and conceding just four.

In Serie A, the Lariani have collected a club record 23 points from their first 10 fixtures, and few would rule them out of vying for the Scudetto.

Though Inter captain Lautaro Martinez is not due back until after the break, and Luis Henrique is also ruled out, the hosts can welcome back a trio of players.

Benjamin Pavard has joined English pair John Stones and Curtis Jones in resuming full training, and they could all make the bench this weekend.

Furthermore, Alessandro Bastoni - who scored in last week's Milan derby - is available after serving a UEFA suspension against Feyenoord.

Up front, Pio Esposito has just netted his first club goal since September, while Marcus Thuram has previously scored four in three league games against Como.

The visitors also boast a potent attack, as Douvikas and star man Nico Paz already have nine Champions League strikes between them.

That pair have been similarly productive in Serie A, with 11 goal involvements combined, but Douvikas has failed to find the net in five prior games against Inter.

Once again, Fabregas will be without Moise Kean, Trevoh Chalobah, Jesus Rodriguez, Jayden Addai and Assane Diao due to injury.

J. Martinez; Bisseck, Akanji, Bastoni; Spence, Barella, Calhanoglu, Zielinski, Dimarco; Thuram, Esposito

Butez; Couto, Kempf, Ramon, Kaiki; Perrone, Milla; Da Cunha, Paz, Baturina; Douvikas

Inter's defence is creaking at the seams, and without the leadership of their inspirational skipper they are always more vulnerable.

Although free-flowing Como must be starting to tire, recent events suggest it is time to finally slay the Nerazzurri.

#1988. Marcus Rashford names player closest to Lionel Messi's level

By Naim Beneddra | 06 Nov 2026 16:57

Manchester United forward Marcus Rashford has named Lamine Yamal as the most talented footballer he has played alongside, suggesting that the Barcelona teenager could eventually come close to matching Lionel Messi's extraordinary achievements.

The England international spent the 2025-26 campaign on loan at Barcelona, where he developed a close appreciation of Yamal's abilities before returning to Old Trafford during the summer.

Despite having shared a dressing room with some of football's biggest names, including Cristiano Ronaldo and Harry Kane, Rashford believes the 19-year-old possesses a level of natural talent unlike anything he has previously encountered.

Speaking during a question-and-answer session with Manchester United supporters at Old Trafford, the 29-year-old revealed that he had personally told Yamal how highly he rated him before leaving Barcelona.

Rashford went even further by suggesting that the Spanish international could end his career with seven Ballon d'Or awards, an achievement that would place him within touching distance of Messi's record.

Rashford's comments came during an appearance in Manchester United's Ambassadors' Lounge ahead of Tuesday's Champions League meeting with Roma.

The forward, who has been sidelined by injury in recent weeks, was asked about Messi and the prospects of his former Barcelona teammate following the recent Ballon d'Or ceremony.

He explained that he had already spoken directly to Yamal about his abilities before completing his return to Manchester.

"Before I left Barcelona, I told him I'd played with some very talented players, but he was above them all," Rashford said, in comments reported by the Manchester Evening News.

The former Aston Villa loanee was particularly struck by how much Yamal had achieved despite still being a teenager.

"I've never seen a player at that age be as talented as he is," he continued.

"For me, he's the closest somebody can get to the level of Messi over the years."

The comparison carries considerable weight given Rashford's experience at the highest level.

He played alongside Ronaldo during the Portuguese star's second spell at Manchester United and has also shared the pitch with Kane for England.

However, Rashford's assessment was focused on Yamal's exceptional ability at such a young age, rather than suggesting that the Barcelona winger has already surpassed those established stars in terms of career achievements.

The United attacker also made clear that he still considers Messi an almost impossible standard to replicate.

Describing the eight-time Ballon d'Or winner as a complete footballing genius, Rashford acknowledged that another player with the Argentine's full range of abilities may never emerge.

Nevertheless, his admiration for Yamal's potential was unmistakable.

The England international believes the Barcelona youngster possesses the talent to remain among the world's leading players for many years, provided he continues developing at his current rate.

Rashford's prediction about Yamal's future went beyond comparing his playing style and natural ability with Messi.

The Manchester United forward suggested that the teenager could eventually collect seven Ballon d'Or trophies.

"If he goes on to win seven Ballons d'Or, I wouldn't be surprised," Rashford explained.

It was a remarkable assessment of a player who has yet to win the senior award but has already finished among its leading contenders on three occasions.

Yamal placed eighth in 2024, finished runner-up to Ousmane Dembele in 2025 and took third place in October's 2026 ceremony, behind winner Harry Kane and Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappe.

He also collected his third consecutive Kopa Trophy last month, having won the award for the world's best young player in 2024 and 2025.

The Barcelona star's rapid rise has been accompanied by major collective success.

He played a central role in Spain's Euro 2024 triumph before helping his country win the 2026 World Cup, while also establishing himself as one of the most influential players in Hansi Flick's Barcelona side.

At club level, Yamal has already become a regular match-winner, combining exceptional dribbling ability with increasingly productive contributions in front of goal.

Rashford also took the opportunity to congratulate Kane on his Ballon d'Or success, revealing that he had sent the Bayern Munich striker a personal message after the ceremony.

The United forward felt that Kane's outstanding goalscoring record and creative output made him a deserving winner of the prestigious award.

His support for Kane did not diminish his enthusiasm about Yamal's future, with Rashford clearly viewing the Spaniard's best years as still to come.

For Rashford himself, the comments offer an insight into the lasting impression left by his season in Catalonia.

Barcelona declined to activate the purchase option in his loan agreement, leading to his return to Manchester United, where he is attempting to revive his career under Michael Carrick.

His admiration for Yamal, however, has evidently remained undiminished.

Having witnessed the teenager's qualities at close quarters, Rashford believes the Barcelona number 10 has the potential to build a career that invites comparisons with the greatest players the sport has produced.

#1985. ‘I like him a lot’ – Romelu Lukaku has been mindblown by Liverpool player he could face tonight

Romelu Lukaku has joined the ever-growing fan club of teenage Liverpool winger Rio Ngumoha, having been impressed by what he’s seen from the 18-year-old.

The youngster has earned widespread praise for his effervescent performances since breaking into the Reds’ first team last year and has started all three Champions League games so far under Andoni Iraola.

He had to be content with 25 minutes or so off the bench against Arsenal on Sunday and was kept quiet by a sturdy Gunners defence, but his direct running has left an impression on the experienced Belgian striker, who he’ll face tonight in our European clash against Fenerbahce.

Lukaku was speaking to TNT Sports ahead of the fixture at the Sukru Saracoglu Stadium, and he highlighted the threat that Liverpool pose in midfield and attack, with the 33-year-old singling out Ngumoha for praise.

The ex-Manchester United and Everton marksman said: “Offensively they are very good as well. I like Rio. I like him a lot, very direct. I saw his game that he played against Arsenal.”

Ngumoha gave arguably his best Liverpool performance in their most recent Champions League outing, the 4-3 win over Villarreal a fortnight ago when he tormented the LaLiga side in completing seven out of the eight dribbles that he attempted (Sofascore).

In many ways he’s almost the antithesis of Lukaku, who’s a towering target man more renowned for power than pace, but the Fenerbahce striker is no less admiring of the teenage winger’s qualities.

#1984. Next Crystal Palace manager: Thomas Tuchel’s stance on Anthony Barry is clear amid Pierre Sage uncertainty

By Oliver Thomas | 06 Nov 2026 17:00

England manager Thomas Tuchel has responded to speculation linking his assistant coach Anthony Barry with the Crystal Palace job.

Barry, 40, is reportedly among the frontrunners to succeed current Eagles boss Pierre Sage if the struggling Selhurst Park outfit decide to relieve the Frenchman of his duties.

Sage replaced Oliver Glasner in June, but his Crystal Palace side currently sit inside the Premier League relegation zone after losing six of their opening nine games and conceding a division-high 21 goals.

Should the Eagles lose at home to Liverpool on Sunday, the club’s hierarchy may have a big decision to make over whether to stick with under-pressure Sage or bring in a fresh face to turn the club’s fortunes around.

While Tuchel - who announced his latest England squad on Friday - is hopeful that Barry will remain his number two, he is not surprised to see the “highest-level coach” linked with Premier League clubs.

“He’s very important to me,” the German told BBC Radio 5 Live. “I mean, that’s why I did everything I could to convince him to join my staff once we met in Chelsea and join me on my way to Bayern Munich and then in the national team.

“It’s a privilege for me to have him by my side. He’s challenging me, he’s helping me, he makes me better.

“He’s just a fantastic person and the highest-level coach, so I am not surprised that there are rumours around him. I’m not surprised if there were like possibilities for him.”

Barry’s contract with the Football Association runs until the end of the European Championship in 2028 when England will co-host the tournament.

“My understanding, my wish is, of course, that we stay together until minimum until the Euros,” Tuchel added.

“For me, we are by far not finished, and he will always have a place in my in my coaching staff, also after the Euros.

“But, listen, he has to follow also his own path. At the moment, I think that we are an excellent team, and I think that he feels that he’s in a good place where he wants to be.

“As soon as this changes, I think I will be the first to know. At the moment, I don’t know nothing, so I’m pretty confident that he’s in a good place, but I’m not surprised that he has offers.”

Although Barry has never been a senior first-team manager before, he has a wealth of experience as an assistant coach, predominantly working under Tuchel at Chelsea, Bayern Munich and now England.

The Liverpudlian began his coaching career at Accrington Stanley and Wigan Athletic, while he also gained international experience with the Republic of Ireland, Belgium and Portugal, working under Roberto Martinez with the latter two nations.

As well as Barry, Sean Dyche, Thomas Frank, Vitor Pereira and Rob Edwards have been linked with the Crystal Palace job amid uncertainty over Sage’s long-term future.

#1983. Man United injury news: Michael Carrick blow, Liverpool boost as key star set to miss Anfield game after international break

By Lewis Nolan | 06 Nov 2026 17:07

Manchester United's Carlos Baleba will miss his side's clash with fierce rivals Liverpool after the international break, Michael Carrick has confirmed.

The Red Devils are set to face Aston Villa on Sunday in the Premier League, but they know they will be without key players for that clash.

Baleba was forced off in the second half of his side's game against Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday due to a hamstring injury.

In a press conference, Carrick confirmed that the midfielder would be out for a considerable period, and that he would be on the treatment table beyond the international break.

That news will come as a significant blow to United, who have to face Liverpool at Anfield on November 22 in the Premier League.

Carrick did not give an exact timeline on Baleba's recovery, but he did reveal that he would miss weeks of action.

United have to face Liverpool after the international break, before taking on Sporting Lisbon three days later in Europe.

Before the start of December, the Red Devils also have to take on Brentford, while the club will also face Newcastle United, Coventry City and RB Leipzig in the first eight days of next month.

Carrick's side end December with fixtures against Crystal Palace, Arsenal, Nottingham Forest and Sunderland, though perhaps Baleba would be ready to feature in at least some of those games.

United finished in third place last season with 71 points, 11 more than Liverpool managed, and the Merseysiders were arguably fortunate to accumulate as many as they did.

However, a loss against Villa and a defeat at Anfield could leave the Red Devils trailing their rivals by 14 points after just 11 matchweeks.

Baleba is arguably Carrick's only competent midfielder without the ball, and missing him at Anfield makes taking any points from that match much more challenging.

United's inability to make the most of the fact that Liverpool and several other teams like Tottenham Hotspur, Chelsea and Manchester City are in transition is concerning.

Losing against Liverpool would compound the failure of the club's hierarchy, and it would arguably be one of the darkest chapters in United's modern history if a loss dropped them into the relegation zone.
